vehicle.mass_note: Measured with setup wheel adapters, 75kg driver, 35kg fuel. Adapters cancel in ratios.

corner_weights.note: RR calculated: total - FL - FR - RL. Measured on setup patch including adapters.

vehicle.yaw_inertia_note: Estimated from Iz = m*a*b bicycle model approximation. Error ~10-20%. Replace with homologation value when available.
vehicle.yaw_inertia_kalman_note: NOT sourced, reviewer placeholder, replace with team figure (same convention as cog_height_m below). WP-S4 diagnostics-only Kalman sideslip observer candidate (diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py) -- deliberately a separate value from vehicle.yaw_inertia_kgm2 (2082.0, production Modules 4a/5's m*a*b bicycle estimate) so this diagnostic does not silently inherit or couple to the production Iz figure. Not consumed by any modules/ production path.
vehicle.steering_ratio_note: Read from steering ratio lookup table at centre wheel travel and zero steering stroke. Treated as constant at Level 1.
vehicle.cog_note: Derived from static weight distribution. a = L * rear_fraction, b = L * front_fraction.
vehicle.cog_height_note: Reviewer-supplied order-of-magnitude placeholder, NOT sourced, replace with team figure.
vehicle.track_width_note: Reviewer-supplied order-of-magnitude placeholder, NOT sourced, replace with team figure.

aero.air_density_note: ISA sea-level standard value. Kept at Level 1 by convention like wheelbase_m -- not a sourced-vs-placeholder distinction, a fixed physical constant that would only move for a session weather correction (not implemented).
aero.lift_coeff_note: Sign convention verified against the chair's own formula (docs/literature/data_handler.py:1559, fz_aero_total_N = -0.5*rho*v^2*A*Cl, commented 'positive for downforce'): since -0.5*rho*v^2*A is never positive, Cl must be NEGATIVE for a downforce-generating car under this convention -- standard aerodynamic lift-coefficient sign (positive=lift, negative=downforce), not a 'downforce coefficient' convention where downforce would read positive. No numeric Cl default exists in the shared reference files to confirm against directly; this is inferred from the formula+comment pairing alone, not an assumed value. Placeholder 0.0: the aero term evaluates to exactly zero at every speed, i.e. Fz reduces to the static+longitudinal-only estimate -- a documented underestimate of both axles' load at speed, not a front/rear balance error. When populated with a real (negative) Cl, re-verify sign against a high-speed straight-line sample (fz_f_N+fz_r_N should exceed the static sum, not fall below it). This sign convention is INFERRED from the formula+comment pairing, not confirmed against a real value -- the first real Cl entry must be validated empirically (Fz increasing with v^2, not decreasing) before being trusted.
aero.cross_track_area_note: Not sourced -- inert while lift_coeff=0.0 (multiplies to zero regardless). Must be sourced together with a real lift_coeff before either has a numeric effect.
aero.diff_cog_x_note: CoP-to-CoG longitudinal offset. Not sourced, inert while lift_coeff=0.0. 0.0 also has a standalone physical meaning if ever populated alone: aero centre of pressure coincides with CoG, i.e. no front/rear aero balance shift.

stability_estimation._comment_sideslip_source: WP-N2 Step 1b (2026-08-20): selects which beta feeds Modules 4b/5 at the ui/views/outing_form.py StabilityAnalysisThread call site. 'kinematic' = production estimate_sideslip (default, byte-identical to every prior session). 'ekf_pass_1' = diagnostics/sideslip_ekf_dugoff.py's pass_1 configuration (frozen Dugoff curve, calibrated noise model, carried forward per thesis_notes.md 'WP-N2 carry-forward decision: pass 1'). Traces (CS_ratio, tyre curve, stability) are meaningful under ekf_pass_1 immediately; verdict thresholds are NOT re-derived for it -- see classification.thresholds_calibrated_for_sideslip_source below. Flip back to 'kinematic' to isolate a regression; no code edit needed either way.
stability_estimation._comment_gps_course_anchor: WP5b(c), estimate_sideslip_gps (validation-only, no pipeline call site). Drift-correction anchor gate: a sample qualifies once a short-window-smoothed |ay| stays below max_ay_g for a contiguous run of at least min_duration_s. Data-derived on Dubai (diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py): raw per-sample |ay| is too noisy for a literal unbroken-run test (2267 candidate runs at the chosen threshold, longest ~0.1s) -- smooth_window_s=0.3 first was necessary to get physically-sized runs (6 runs >=1.5s, 20.4s total anchor time across 4 laps). max_ay_g=0.05 sits at the moving-sample |ay| p10 (0.044g), a natural low-|ay| population before the distribution rises steeply toward cornering values (p20=0.109g).
stability_estimation.gps_course_latency_s_derived_from: diagnostics/inspect_beta_gps_validation.py, WP5b(c) iteration 1 Section 0: cross-correlation of wrap-safe d(course)/dt against -yaw_rate_radps over lags -1..+1s (racing laps, moving samples) peaks at r=0.9898 at lag=+0.32s, vs r=0.9575 at zero lag -- course-derived rotation consistently lags yaw_rate by this much. A stale course reading recorded at time t describes the vehicle's true state at (t - latency); querying it at (t + latency) recovers the value that actually corresponds to the query instant.
stability_estimation._comment_yaw_stability: Module 5 estimator (modules/yaw_stability.py), after the chair performance_analysis tooling (internal). These are the values the chair pipeline actually runs (its dataclass defaults / default invocation) -- changing any of the six re-triggers classification-threshold re-derivation (WP5b(e) pattern), since thresholds are tuned to this estimator's output distribution.
stability_estimation._comment_cs_fallback: Fallback cornering stiffness references. Derived from axle normal load × C_alpha/Fz = 12 rad⁻¹ (Milliken & Milliken, RCVD, GT3 slick). Front: (290+290)*9.81*12 = 68268. Rear: (395+381)*9.81*12 = 91343. Used as C_linear_ref when OLS cannot resolve the linear stiffness from data (insufficient alpha excitation on rear axle). Accuracy Level 1. RE-INTRODUCED 2026-08-19 (WP-S4): deleted 2026-07-26 as consumed nowhere in modules/ (thesis_notes.md 'Small-decisions sweep'); re-added verbatim (same values, same original comment above) as the tyre-stiffness prior for diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py's Kalman sideslip observer candidate (circularity option 2, beta-independent prior -- a fixed, non-alpha-derived Caf/Car instead of the alpha-circular windowed OLS stiffness). Still not consumed by any modules/ production path, diagnostics-only.

tyre_model_fit._comment: WP-N1 (diagnostics/fit_dugoff_first_pass.py only -- no modules/ consumer yet). Calibration tunable defining the low-|ay| population treated as the near-linear tyre regime for the Dugoff c_alpha first-pass fit (Fy vs kinematic alpha, through the origin). Not yet re-derived from a data-driven gap-selection pass -- 0.3g is the WP's stated default, carried forward from the WP-N0 saturation-coverage diagnostic's own candidate-threshold list.

tyre_model_ekf._comment: pass 0: nonlinear Dugoff single-track EKF (diagnostics/sideslip_ekf_dugoff.py). Diagnostics-only, no modules/ consumer. pass_0's c_alpha/mu_fz are COPIED (not re-read live) from the tyre_model_fit result (diagnostics/fit_dugoff_first_pass.py's Module-4b-seeded fit); full derivation and circularity status recorded in thesis_notes.md. A future refit of tyre_model_fit therefore cannot silently change what pass 0 was defined as -- a numbered pass must be fully reproducible from its own recorded parameters alone.

pass_0.frozen_from: WP-N1b, diagnostics/fit_dugoff_first_pass_manifest.json (timestamp 2026-08-19T14:00:40Z) -- Module-4b-median c_alpha, interior-optimum mu_fz fit. fz_accuracy_level Level 1, Cl=0 -- effective mu (1.90 front / 2.06 rear) conditional on this, same caveat the manifest itself carries.
pass_0.seeded_from: diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py, tuned linear Kalman observer, QR_RATIO=0.3162 (WP-S5b 7-point ratio sweep). Starting point only: a linear KF's gain is provably invariant under uniform (Q,R,P) rescaling, but this EKF's Jacobian is state-dependent (through the tyre model's local slope, which falls toward zero near saturation) and that invariance is NOT assumed to transfer. A same-ratio, different-absolute-scale rerun is proposed as the first sensitivity check, in the validation work package -- not run this pass.
pass_0.beta_hard_bound_note: Physically anchored, NOT derived from the kinematic estimate's own observed beta range -- that estimate under-reads mid-corner (thesis_notes.md, 'Linear observer' entries), so its range would clip the very signal this filter exists to recover. Controlled racing sideslip on this class of car stays well below 15 deg; a genuinely diverged filter exceeds it by orders of magnitude.
pass_0.nis_tuning_note: nis_window_samples, nis_chi2_bound (chi-square 95% bound, df=2) and nis_flag_fraction are PLACEHOLDER defaults (20 samples = ~0.4s at 50Hz; majority-of-window), not yet data-derived against a real pass-0 run -- that is the next work package (validation script), not this one.
pass_0.Iz_provenance: vehicle.yaw_inertia_kgm2 (2082.0) used in this filter's r_dot, NOT vehicle.yaw_inertia_kalman_kgm2 (1800.0). Chosen because modules/stability_analysis.py estimate_lateral_forces built the Fy_f/Fy_r that this pass's frozen c_alpha/mu_fz were fit against (WP-N1b) using yaw_inertia_kgm2=2082.0 -- using 1800.0 here would make the filter's own moment balance inconsistent with its training data's Iz by ~14%. Both values remain Level-1 estimates/placeholders in their own right (yaw_inertia_kgm2: m*a*b bicycle-model approximation, ~10-20% error, vehicle.yaw_inertia_note; yaw_inertia_kalman_kgm2: unsourced reviewer placeholder) -- 2082.0 is chosen for self-consistency with the training data, not claimed to be the more accurate of the two.
pass_0.fy_axle_dependency_note: Fy_f/Fy_r (estimate_lateral_forces) satisfy a*Fy_f - b*Fy_r == Iz*psidd_raw IDENTICALLY (a=cog_to_front_axle_m, b=cog_to_rear_axle_m derived from the same static corner-weight split as front/rear_fraction; psidd_raw=np.gradient(yaw_rate_radps)) -- verified numerically on Dubai data using a/b computed live from wheelbase*fraction (max abs deviation 7.3e-12 Nm, floating-point noise only). Using the config's own stored (3-decimal-rounded) cog_to_front/rear_axle_m instead gives a small nonzero residual (max 21.1 Nm, mean 5.4 Nm, median relative deviation 0.43% against a 645 Nm floor) fully explained by that rounding, not by any additional independent measurement. Consequence: Fy_f and Fy_r together carry exactly two independent measured quantities (ay and yaw-rate-derivative/psidd), not four independent per-axle numbers -- any fit against both axle forces inherits this coupling, and this must not be read as two independently-corroborating force channels.
pass_0.changed_from_previous: n/a -- first pass. Dugoff c_alpha/mu_fz newly fit (WP-N1b); Q/R/P0 newly seeded from the rejected linear KF observer (see seeded_from) -- both tyre curve and noise model are new here, there being no prior pass to diff against.

pass_1.changed_from_previous: noise model only; Dugoff c_alpha/mu_fz unchanged from pass_0. R_ay_var/R_yaw_rate_var reflect the completed 2-D sweep refinement (r_q_sweep_note), not just the initial single-shot derivation -- still the same noise-model-only pass, refined in place rather than renumbered, since the tyre curve and Q are untouched throughout.
pass_1.frozen_from: Identical to pass_0 -- copied, not refit this pass. See pass_0.frozen_from for the WP-N1b provenance.
pass_1.seeded_from: Q and P0 copied unchanged from pass_0 -- no non-arbitrary single-shot derivation exists for Q without a Q-focused sweep, still not run (nothing so far implicates Q specifically; see r_q_sweep_note). R redefined to represent TOTAL INNOVATION UNCERTAINTY (sensor noise plus tyre-model error), not accelerometer/gyro precision alone -- pass_0's R assumed 0.05 m/s^2 (ay) / 0.1 deg/s (yaw rate) sensor-only noise while the Dugoff fit's own RMS residuals (WP-N1b) are 2.0/4.3 m/s^2-equivalent per axle, two orders of magnitude larger; trusting the measurement update to sensor precision when the model itself is that wrong is what produced pass_0's 93.4% combined NIS exceedance and the C2 excursion. Full rationale: thesis_notes.md, WP-N2 Q/R recalibration entry.
pass_1.R_ay_derivation: SUPERSEDED by r_q_sweep_note below, history kept for the record. Original single-shot derivation (Method A, fit-residual-based, non-circular): WP-N1b per-axle Dugoff fit RMS residuals (front 2752.7 N, rear 5793.2 N over the SAME base_mask population, n=24183) converted to acceleration (front 2.030, rear 4.272 m/s^2). Independence was checked, not assumed: correlation(resid_front, resid_rear) = 0.8999 (materially correlated) -- combined via the correlated formula, giving combined std=6.1516 m/s^2 (R_ay_var=37.8418), vs 4.7197 m/s^2 (R_ay_var=22.2757) under the independence assumption that was checked and rejected. Method B (direct empirical innovation from an actual pass-0 run, std=1.864 m/s^2, R_ay_var=3.475) was measured too but NOT used as the original derivation -- it is contaminated by pass_0's own wrong R distorting the state trajectory; demoted to a post-hoc convergence check instead. That first-derivation value (R_ay_var=37.8418) was RUN and found to over-correct the ay channel (0.04% NIS exceedance, Kalman gain's ay column collapsed ~180x vs pass_0) -- see r_q_sweep_note for the resolution.
pass_1.R_yaw_rate_derivation: SUPERSEDED by r_q_sweep_note below, history kept for the record. Original derivation, sequenced after R_ay (not simultaneously, to avoid conflating yaw-rate's own model error with a knock-on effect of the ay miscalibration corrupting the shared 2-state update): yaw-rate innovation std was 3.1709 deg/s at pass_0 (R_ay still wrong); after fixing R_ay alone (interim run, R_yaw_rate/Q still at pass_0 values) it dropped to 2.2278 deg/s -- confirming part of the original inflation WAS a knock-on effect, but a substantial independent residual remained. That first-derivation value (R_yaw_rate_var=0.001511889) was RUN and found to under-correct (30.1% NIS exceedance, above the 15% gate) -- see r_q_sweep_note for the resolution.
pass_1.r_q_sweep_note: The two single-shot derivations above landed the two channels on OPPOSITE sides of the 3%-15% NIS-exceedance gate (ay too low at 0.04%, yaw rate too high at 30.1%) -- a scalar rescale of R as a whole cannot fix an imbalance between its own two diagonal entries, so a 2-D grid over (R_ay_scale, R_yaw_rate_scale), each independently multiplying this pass's own first-derivation values, was run instead of restarting from scratch (diagnostics/inspect_ekf_pass1_rQ_sweep.py, Q held fixed -- nothing diagnosed so far implicates Q specifically). Of 25 grid points (R_ay_scale in [1,0.3,0.1,0.03,0.01], R_yaw_scale in [1,2,4,8,16]), exactly one landed both channels inside [3%,15%]: R_ay_scale=0.1 (R_ay_var=3.78418, yaw_exceed=10.0%), R_yaw_scale=4.0 (R_yaw_rate_var=0.0060476, ay_exceed=9.2%) -- the values now stored above. Notable cross-check: R_ay_scale=0.1 lands within 9% of Method B's earlier-demoted empirical estimate (R_ay_var=3.475) -- the contamination concern that demoted Method B was real in principle but turned out not to be a large practical distortion for this specific number.

REAR mu_fz FIT DID NOT CONVERGE TO AN INTERIOR OPTIMUM -- the bounded least-squares search hit its widened bracket ceiling after 4 widen attempts (mu_fz_bound_fraction=0.99999998), landing at mu_fz_rear=8484797 N, effective mu=1102.5 -- PHYSICALLY IMPLAUSIBLE, failure mode 3 as pre-registered in the WP-N2 pass 2 proposal. pass_4.frozen_from: WP-N2 pass 4, diagnostics/fit_dugoff_pass4_refit.py, diagnostics/fit_dugoff_pass4_refit_manifest.json (timestamp 2026-08-20T08:34:44Z). Front is a normal two-step fit, same shape as every prior pass.
pass_4.mu_fz_rear_fit_failure_note: The mu_fz least-squares objective only constrains mu_fz through samples where the Dugoff model actually saturates (lambda=mu_fz/(2*c_alpha*|tan(alpha)|) < 1); c_alpha_rear this pass (114873, close to pass_3's 118729, essentially unchanged) combined with this pass's alpha population apparently leaves few or no samples demanding saturation at any mu_fz the search bracket could represent before widening ran out, so the optimizer drove mu_fz to the bracket ceiling instead of finding a true minimum. Consequence: the rear Dugoff curve this pass is effectively PURE LINEAR (Fy_r = c_alpha_rear*tan(alpha_r), no representable saturation) across the visited alpha range -- structurally the same failure mode (cannot represent saturation) that condemned the linear Kalman observer earlier in this arc, arrived at here via a degenerate fit rather than a deliberately linear model choice. See thesis_notes.md WP-N2 pass 4 entry for the full diagnosis and the decision to stop iteration here.

Supersedes -500.0 (time-anchored OLS estimator, removed B1, see thesis_notes.md). Re-derive if yaw_stability_* above changes. Confirmed unchanged 2026-07-24 (Module 5 independent of Fy/Fz, distribution byte-identical). Re-confirmed 2026-07-26: exceedances identical, id-8 cluster and -99.3/-18.8 gap intact. Re-confirmed 2026-07-27 after WP1 canonical consolidation + boundary partition: stability gap now -398/+25 (C8-only negative population, exceedance 4/4/4 unchanged); CS moderate-count drops traceable to repaired realization defects (C11 misclassification, window jitter), not drift -- realization-accuracy upgrade, values kept.

accuracy_levels._comment: Single source of truth for per-quantity accuracy (1=config default, 2=session measurement, 3=logged sensor, 4=lookup table; upgrade each node independently, CLAUDE.md/thesis_notes.md). Each node: level (current STATIC/default tier, what a run with no session data resolves to), source (what currently provides the value), capped_by (why it isn't higher: 'chained-constant: <name>' when a Level-1 config constant sits in the node's own derivation chain, 'provenance-assumption: <name>' when no such constant exists but a documented, unverifiable assumption about the channel's own measurement caps it anyway, or null when neither mechanism applies). Consolidated 2026-07-26 -- see thesis_notes.md for the yaw_rate=3 vs steering_angle=1 resolution evidence. WP-C (2026-07-26) adds per-session dynamic resolution on top of this static registry, in modules/accuracy_resolution.py: leaf nodes (mass, corner_weights, and in future WPs steering_ratio/speed/sideslip_angle) carry a real ordered source list there and resolve independently per outing; derived nodes have no source list of their own and instead cascade from the nodes named in capped_by -- either a PURE cascade (resolved level = input's resolved level exactly, e.g. cog_position from corner_weights) or a METHOD-CEILINGED cascade bounded by an explicit method_ceiling field below (the derivation is itself an approximation whose error a better-measured input cannot shrink, e.g. yaw_inertia's m*a*b formula). Every node not dynamically wired yet stays single-source at its level below regardless of any global cap, until its own future WP gives it a second source.

yaw_inertia_kalman.note: WP-S4 diagnostics-only Kalman sideslip observer candidate (diagnostics/sideslip_kalman_observer.py); not consumed by any production Module 2-6 path. Distinct node from yaw_inertia (production, vehicle.yaw_inertia_kgm2) -- deliberately not chained to it.

steering_ratio.source: config default (vehicle.steering_ratio); dynamically resolves to Level 4 (car_data.json steering_ratio_table, manufacturer digitised) when that local-only file is present and the cap allows it -- modules/accuracy_resolution.py. Parameterization, not a chair-comparison deviation: the constant was never a chair scientific position, it is this car's own mechanical steering geometry.

sideslip_angle.note: GPS-course L3 path investigated (WP5b(c), two iterations, 2026-07-26): NOT viable on this dataset - diagnosed scale-drift corrected and corroborated, remaining error not dominated by it; shelved pending denser anchor data (longer session / more straights). See thesis_notes. Kinematic beta remains production.

speed.capped_by: provenance-assumption: opaque ECU wheel-speed calibration (thesis_notes.md limitations register item 10)
speed.note: GPS speed cross-validation investigated (WP5b(d), 2026-07-26): diagnostic/validation only, NOT switched to production -- ecu_speed remains the production source and pipeline time-anchor throughout. Measured a consistent origin-regression scale factor k=1.012 (ecu_speed reads ~1.2% low vs GPS, tight across speed classes, braking/traction slip prediction NOT confirmed as the dominant driver of the offset -- see thesis_notes) -- a candidate rolling-radius correction to ecu_speed's own conversion. MEASURING k is not itself an estimator-input change; APPLYING it would be (v feeds Modules 2-5 and the aero-Fz term), and is a separate future decision with its own re-derivation stop, not taken here. See thesis_notes.

yaw_rate.source: sclu_yaw_rate logged channel, exact rpm-to-radps unit conversion

steering_angle.source: log_asteer logged channel, converted via steering_ratio (pure cascade -- resolves to steering_ratio's own resolved level, WP-B)

lateral_acc.source: log_acc_y logged channel, exact g-to-mps2 unit conversion

wheelbase_m.note: Fixed chassis dimension, known to design tolerance; not expected to move enough to justify a dedicated remeasurement -- kept at Level 1 by convention, not as a live upgrade target.
